page0.text:
...She hears a voice.
Her body is in tatters and her mind is a haze, but she hears a voice that she didn't want to hear.

page1.text: "I don't know if it's mutual, but I've known about you for quite a while, Shirou."

page2.text:
She doesn't consider why she can hear their conversation.
She just wishes that she couldn't.
If she could move her hands, she'd cover her ears. If she could move her legs, she would go to the living room and put a stop to this.

page3.text: "I was watching, right after I came out of the building. I saw some boy at the edge of campus trying over and over to jump a bar that was too high for him, like a moron."

page4.text:
"...Ngh."
The girl bites her lip.
Her sluggish fingers clench the bedsheets hard enough to tear them.
The old story her sister recounts in a disinterested tone—
The sight on the school yard that evening, four years ago—
Rin is talking about the memory like it only belongs to her.
Like it's something that only she knew about.
She's lost in a beautiful memory, even though she/I didn't even know I/she was there.

page5.text:
"Stop. Please, stop. I'm begging you, don't..."
Don't take this memory from me, the girl begs.
With an inaudible voice, she squeezes out a plea that no one can hear.

page6.text:
Her sister continues telling the tale.
The girl is getting left behind, just as she feared.
It was the only thing.
That memory was the one and only precious thing she had over her big sister, who was now treating it like any other memory.

page7.text:
"No... No, no, no...!"
She reinforces her frayed nerves with her power—her mind, and covers both ears with her hands.
She doesn't want to hear it.
This is torture.
Why, why, why does she know what's happening in the living room?
Does her shadow stretch that far?
No, never mind that, she doesn't want to hear anything.
No more.
If she hears any more, she has a feeling she'll go insane.

page8.text:
Still, she can't block out the conversation, even as she covers her ears.
Her sister's words echo straight into her brain.
She can cover her ears and gouge out her eyes, but she can't escape that sight.
And then...

page9.text:
"Shirou. When it comes down to it, I'm going to kill her. It's the best way for both of us.
You need to think about that, too."

page10.text:
Her sister coldly thrust those
words she least wanted to hear
at the last person she wanted to hear them.

page11.text:
And then she couldn't hear their voices anymore.
She can't tell what's happening in the living room.
...Of course not.
Her world consists only of this dark room.
She can't step into that distant, bright world.

page12.text:
...
...Her eyelids feel warm.
She realizes she's been crying on her own.
She's sad and frustrated.

page13.text:
Her sister is a coward.
Why, why is she forcing the obvious conclusion on Senpai?
Because it's her duty as the Tohsaka mage? Then she can fulfill it on her own. Why pull Senpai into it?
My sister is trying to make my Senpai, my one and only ally in the whole world, stand with her.

page14.text:
"Nee...san."
...Hate.
She knows how self-centered it sounds, but she hates her.
She's going to make Senpai abandon Sakura Matou.
Rin Tohsaka is truly cruel for doing that.

page15.text:
"...Nee-san."
...But, it's strange.
Why do I hate her so much, when it's what I want?
Nee-san said I should just disappear.
I know that, and I agree.
...I can't remember the details anymore, but I do know that Shirou Emiya would be saved if I was gone.

page16.text:
"...No. I don't want to."
I can't.
I don't want to lose anything else.
I don't want to be alone anymore.
I know warmth now, so I'm afraid of the cold.
I know warmth now, so I hate everyone who's been warm this whole time.
...I won't disappear for them.
...I won't let them kill me.
Because, because...

page18.text:
Everyone else is wrong.
I never wanted this outcome.
It only happened because nobody helped me.
So...if nobody did anything to help me, that means they wanted it to happen.
They weren't against "me." That's the same as agreeing with me.
In that case...
Nobody will punish me. They couldn't if they tried.

page19.text:
"...I won't die. Not the way she wants."
...No.
The actual problem is that I can't die.
Nobody can kill me.
If they're going to, I'm okay with that.
If I'm going to be killed—I'll—instead.

page20.text:
Not just my sister.
Even Senpai. If they try to erase me, I won't put up with it anymore.
...Yeah.
If they're going to hate me and go far away, then I'd rather...
—Senpai with my own hands before he ends up with someone else, just like in my nightmares—

page21.text:
"Ah... Haah, ugh!"
She coughs.
Painfully, she turns her delusions into blood, expelling it from her mouth.

page22.text:
"...Oh, no. I think I'm no good anymore, Senpai."
Nothing connects.
She doesn't know what's good or bad.
She doesn't know if she's right or wrong.
Who am I? How much sanity do I have left? Everything's getting so foggy, I feel like I'm going mad.

page23.text:
"Hi. Are you still there, Sakura?"
And then...
She realizes there's a silver-haired girl standing there.
She's just like her.
A pale girl who was never treated as human, meant to become a vessel.

page24.text:
"Saber, Lancer, Caster, Berserker.
Those four alone would have been plenty. Where did you find a soul like that? I'm surprised that you're already full when Assassin and Rider are still out there."
...She doesn't know.
She's heard from her grandfather that, just like the girl, she's a container to store the souls of defeated Servants.
But... the implication that Servants other than the ones she was given were defeated is...

page25.text:
"That's good. Now I don't have to worry about Archer getting taken, so I won't press you on it.
Do you know what's going to happen to you now, Sakura?"
...
...She feels something go cold, deep inside her head.
The question pulls Sakura Matou out of her fevered haze.
